mainTopic: Food that shrank and swelled again: is it permanently rejected (יש דיחוי באיסורין)? And whether food is measured by its current size or its original size.
overview: The גמרא first pins down where the dispute really lies: food that had the required size, shrank below it, and then swelled back. One side says the shrinking rejects it for good (יש דיחוי באיסורין), and the other says it does not (אין דיחוי באיסורין). A משנה in טהרות says that shrunken impure foods, and shrunken פיגול, נותר and חלב, become impure and forbidden again once they swell back in the rain. That is a full תיובתא against the 'rejection' view. The גמרא then returns to the main question: is food measured by its current size or its original size? It brings a ברייתא about separating fresh figs for dried figs 'by number' and dried figs for fresh figs 'by measure'. Each half seems to fit only one view, because otherwise the person gives too much tithe and ruins his tithes. The גמרא first answers that the ברייתא is about standard תרומה given generously. The story of רבי יוסי giving ten figs for ninety rules that out. So the גמרא says the case is תרומת מעשר, following אבא אלעזר בן גומל, who holds that תרומת מעשר may be taken by estimate just like standard תרומה. His statement continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Where the dispute really is: food that shrank and then swelled back
steps.stepSummary: The disagreement is about food that had the required size, shrank, and then swelled again. One side holds יש דיחוי באיסורא, and the other holds אין דיחוי באיסורא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only disagree when the food had the full size, shrank, and then swelled back again. One Sage holds that once something is pushed out of a ritual status, it stays out. The other Sage holds that it can come back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows down the earlier argument. It tells us the exact case where the two sides disagree: food that shrank and then grew back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether the time the food was too small counts as a permanent 'rejection' (דיחוי). The side of שמואל, רבי שמעון and ריש לקיש from earlier on the דף holds יש דיחוי, so once the food shrank it can never become impure again. The side of רב, רבי חייא and רבי יוחנן holds אין דיחוי, so when the food swells back, its status returns.

keyTerms.meaning: Rejection: being pushed out of a status permanently
A ritual or prohibition matter (here including טומאה)
The required minimum size
Shrank or shriveled
Swelled up

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the precise idea of דיחוי that the next steps will attack.

phrases.english: When they disagree,
it is in a case where it had the required measure
and it shrank, and then swelled again,
that one Sage holds:
there is rejection in ritual matters,
and the other Sage holds:
there is no rejection in ritual matters.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי פְּלִיגִי, כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיָה בּוֹ כְּשִׁיעוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion on the דף by locating the exact point of disagreement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the dispute to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think they argue about any food that shrank.
steps.terutzMaskana: They only argue about food that shrank and then swelled back, and the argument is over יש or אין דיחוי.

steps.title: Challenge: a משנה says shrunken foods lose their status
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether anyone can really hold יש דיחוי. It quotes a משנה: impure foods, and also פיגול, נותר and חלב, that shrank in the sun lose their impurity and their prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can anyone really say there is rejection in ritual matters? We learned in a משנה: an egg-sized piece of food, an olive-sized piece of a corpse, of a נבלה, of פיגול, of נותר, or of חלב, or a lentil-sized piece of a שרץ, that was left in the sun and shrank, is pure. One is also not liable for it as פיגול, נותר or חלב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts an attack on the view of יש דיחוי by quoting a משנה. This is only the first half of the משנה. The punchline comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the משנה only says that shrunken items lose their status, and both sides agree with that. The challenge is building toward the second half, which deals with what happens when the items swell back.

keyTerms.meaning: An egg-bulk, the minimum size for food to carry טומאה
An olive-bulk, the minimum size for a corpse, a נבלה, and eating prohibitions
A lentil-bulk, the minimum size for שרץ impurity
A קרבן made invalid by a wrong intention about time
Meat of a קרבן left past its time
Forbidden animal fat

phrases.english: And is there anyone who says
that there is rejection in ritual matters?
But didn't we learn in a משנה:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in טהרות 3:6.

phrases.english: an egg-bulk of food
that one placed in the sun and it shrank,
and likewise an olive-bulk from a corpse,
an olive-bulk from an animal carcass,
and a lentil-bulk from a creeping creature,
and an olive-bulk of piggul, and an olive-bulk of notar,
and an olive-bulk of forbidden fat: they are pure,
and one is not liable for them
on account of piggul, notar, or forbidden fat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִיכָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר דְּיֵשׁ דִּיחוּי בְּאִיסּוּרִין? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the יש דיחוי side defined in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that יש דיחוי באיסורין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה will show that shrunken items regain their status when they swell, so there is no permanent rejection.

steps.title: The punchline: when they swell back, the status returns
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: if the shrunken items were put in the rain and swelled, they are impure again. One is also liable again for פיגול, נותר and חלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he then put them in the rain and they swelled back, they are impure. One is liable for them as פיגול, נותר and חלב.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of the משנה, and it is the real force of the challenge. Food that shrank and then grew back gets its old status back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is exactly the case defined in step 1: the food had the full size, shrank, and swelled back. The משנה says the status comes back, so the shrinking did not permanently 'reject' it. That directly contradicts יש דיחוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Rain
Impure
Liable (here, to כרת)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the משנה proves a new rule about the sun. The key point is the rain part: swelling back restores the status, which means there is no permanent rejection.

phrases.english: If he placed them in the rain and they swelled, they are impure,
and one is liable for them
on account of piggul, notar, or forbidden fat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה quoted in step 2 and delivers the actual contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that יש דיחוי באיסורין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Food that shrank and swelled back is impure and forbidden again, so there was no permanent rejection.

steps.title: The 'rejection' view is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares a תיובתא against the view of יש דיחוי באיסורין and confirms that the refutation stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of the one who says there is rejection in ritual matters. Yes, it is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the view of יש דיחוי is knocked down by the משנה, with no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'תיובתא' a second time means the גמרא found no way to defend the view. So the conclusion is that in ritual matters there is no permanent rejection: shrunken food that swells back regains its status.

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusive refutation that has no answer

steps.whatToRemember: A rule to keep: אין דיחוי באיסורין. Food that shrank below the minimum size and then swelled back gets its impurity or prohibition back.

phrases.english: This is a refutation of the one who says
there is rejection in ritual matters!
It is indeed a refutation.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּיוּבְתָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר יֵשׁ דִּיחוּי בְּאִיסּוּרִין! תְּיוּבְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final result of the challenge in steps 2 and 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The view of יש דיחוי באיסורין is refuted. Shrunken food that swells back regains its status.

steps.title: New proof: separating תרומה from fresh figs for dried figs by number
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the main question of whether food is measured by its current size or its original size. It brings a ברייתא: one may separate תרומה from fresh figs for dried figs, but only by number.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: one may separate תרומה from fresh figs to cover dried figs, but only by counting them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to try to settle the main question about measuring food by its current or original size. This is a setup line, and the discussion of what it proves continues after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fresh figs are bigger than dried ones, so measuring by volume would give less תרומה than counting. Requiring 'by number' seems to suggest that the dried figs' smaller current size is not what counts. The next step explains exactly how this proves the point.

keyTerms.meaning: One separates תרומה
Fresh figs
Dried figs
By number, by counting

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One may separate terumah from fresh figs for dried figs,
by number.
phrases.notes: He means counting the figs, not measuring by volume, since fresh figs take up more space than dried ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: תּוֹרְמִין תְּאֵנִים עַל הַגְּרוֹגְרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side question about דיחוי and goes back to the main dispute over current versus original size.
steps.raayaObject: Whether food is measured by its current size or its original size
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about separating תרומה from fresh figs for dried figs, by number

steps.title: The first half of the ברייתא fits only 'original size'
steps.stepSummary: Separating fresh figs for dried figs by number makes sense if we measure by original size. If we measure by current size, the person gives too much.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we measure food by its original size, counting fresh figs against dried figs is fine. But if we measure by current size, the fresh figs are bigger, so he is giving more than he needs to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the first half of the ברייתא seems to prove that we measure food by its original size (לכמות שהן).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dried figs were once as big as fresh figs. If we look at their original size, one fresh fig matches one dried fig, so counting works. If we look at their current, shrunken size, each fresh fig is bigger than a dried one, so counting means giving too much.

keyTerms.meaning: As they were: measured by their original size
As they are: measured by their current size
One who gives more than the required amount of tithes
It works well, granted

steps.confusionAlert: The two phrases look almost the same. לִכְמוֹת שֶׁהֵן (with the ל) means the original size, 'as they were.' כְּמוֹת שֶׁהֵן (without the ל) means the current size, 'as they are now.'

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
that we measure them as they were, it is fine,
phrases.notes: 'As they were' means the original size, before the figs dried and shrank.

phrases.english: but if you say we measure them as they are now,
then he is one who gives too much tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא לִכְמוֹת שֶׁהֵן מְשַׁעֲרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא quoted in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That we measure food by its original size (לכמות שהן)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The first half of the ברייתא: fresh figs for dried figs, by number

steps.title: Giving too much tithe ruins the tithes
steps.stepSummary: A source teaches that if someone gives too much tithe, his produce is fixed but his tithes are ruined. This shows why 'giving too much' is a real problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: if someone gives too much tithe, the rest of his produce is fine to eat, but the tithes themselves are ruined.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to show that giving too much tithe is not harmless. This backs up the proof from step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rest of his food is properly tithed, so he may eat it. The extra portion he called 'tithe' is not really tithe, though, and it was never tithed itself, so his tithes are spoiled. A ברייתא would never instruct someone to do this, so counting by number must not count as giving too much.

keyTerms.meaning: Fixed: properly tithed and allowed to be eaten
Ruined, spoiled

phrases.english: And we learned:
One who gives too much tithe,
his produce is fixed,
but his tithes are ruined.
phrases.notes: The extra amount is not real tithe, and it was never tithed itself, so it is a problem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows why the result in step 6 is unacceptable under the 'current size' view.
steps.raayaObject: Giving too much tithe is a real problem, which strengthens the proof for 'original size'

steps.title: But the second half of the ברייתא says 'by measure'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: are we really measuring by original size? The end of the ברייתא says dried figs for fresh figs must be by measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you really think we measure by original size? Look at the end of the ברייתא: dried figs for fresh figs, by measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back by quoting the last part of the same ברייתא. It is setting up a problem for the 'original size' view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half was about fresh figs for dried figs. The second half reverses the case, dried figs for fresh figs, and requires measuring by volume instead of counting. The next step explains why this hurts the 'original size' view.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the end: look at the last part of the same source
By measure: by volume, not by counting

phrases.english: Rather, what, we measure as they were?
Say the end of the ברייתא:
Dried figs for fresh figs, by measure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי לִכְמוֹת שֶׁהֵן? אֵימָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion drawn in steps 6 and 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof that we measure by original size
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The end of the same ברייתא requires measuring by volume, which seems to point to the 'current size' view.

steps.title: The second half fits only 'current size'
steps.stepSummary: Measuring dried figs by volume makes sense if we measure by current size. If we measure by original size, the person gives too much.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we measure by current size, measuring by volume is fine. But if we measure by original size, each dried fig was once a full fig, so giving them by volume means giving too much.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge. The second half of the ברייתא now causes the same 'too much tithe' problem for the 'original size' view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It takes more dried figs than fresh figs to fill the same volume. If each dried fig counts at its original size, he only needed to give a matching number. Giving by volume means giving extra, which is מרבה במעשרות. The ברייתא now seems to contradict itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Fine, it works well

steps.whatToRemember: The first half of the ברייתא (fresh for dried, by number) fits 'original size.' The second half (dried for fresh, by measure) fits 'current size.' Each view runs into trouble with one half.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the need for a new way to read the ברייתא. Both halves cannot be explained by either view alone.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא כְּמוֹת שֶׁהֵן – שַׁפִּיר,
phrases.english: Granted, if you say we measure them as they are now, it is fine,
but if you say we measure them as they were,
then he is one who gives too much tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא כְּמוֹת שֶׁהֵן – שַׁפִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge opened in step 8, using the same reasoning as step 6 in reverse.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that we measure by original size (לכמות שהן)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under 'original size,' requiring dried figs by volume makes the person give too much tithe, which ruins his tithes.

steps.title: Both clauses are about standard תרומה given generously
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is about תרומה גדולה, and in both clauses the person is choosing to give generously.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the ברייתא is talking about standard תרומה. In the first part the person gives generously, and in the last part he also gives generously.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from Steps 8-9 by saying the ברייתא is not about tithes at all. It is about standard תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tithes need an exact amount, so giving too much is a problem there. Standard תרומה has no fixed Torah amount, so giving a little extra is simply being generous (עין יפה). That way both clauses can involve giving extra, and neither one tells us how food is measured.

keyTerms.meaning: Standard תרומה, the first gift separated from produce for a כהן
Literally 'a good eye'; giving generously
The first clause of a source
The last clause of a source
We are dealing with

phrases.english: Rather, here we are dealing with standard teruma,
phrases.notes: Standard תרומה has no exact Torah amount, so giving extra is allowed.

phrases.english: and the first clause is with a generous eye,
and the last clause is also with a generous eye.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction between the two clauses of the ברייתא by moving the case to standard תרומה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about tithes, where giving too much is a problem, so its clauses contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is about standard תרומה, where giving extra is just generosity. So the ברייתא proves nothing about the measuring question.

steps.title: Ten figs is far too much for standard תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The end of the ברייתא says רבי יוסי gave ten dried figs for ninety fresh ones, which is much more than even generous standard תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the end of the ברייתא. רבי אלעזר son of רבי יוסי said: My father would take ten dried figs from the container for ninety fresh figs in the basket. If this is standard תרומה, why ten?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of Step 10 using the last part of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a generous gift of standard תרומה is about one-fortieth. Ten for ninety is far beyond that. So the story does not fit standard תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; introduces a challenge to the last answer
Basket
What is it doing here? What is its purpose?

phrases.english: If so, say the last clause:
Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yosei said:
Father would take ten dried figs
phrases.notes: Here 'אבא' just means 'my father', which is רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: that were in the container, for ninety that were in the basket,
and if it is about standard teruma,
what are ten doing here?

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא is about standard תרומה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ten for ninety is far more than any normal amount of standard תרומה, even a generous one, so the case cannot be standard תרומה.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about תרומת מעשר and follows אבא אלעזר בן גומל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now says the ברייתא is about תרומת מעשר and follows the view of אבא אלעזר בן גומל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the ברייתא is talking about תרומת מעשר, and it follows the view of אבא אלעזר בן גומל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer: the case is תרומת מעשר, which is one-tenth, so ten figs makes much more sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ten for ninety is close to the one-tenth amount of תרומת מעשר, so the story of רבי יוסי now fits. The גמרא also ties the ברייתא to אבא אלעזר בן גומל, whose view is explained in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: The tenth that a לוי separates from his מעשר and gives to a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'אבא' is part of a name (אבא אלעזר בן גומל), not 'my father' like in Step 11.

phrases.english: Rather, here we are dealing with teruma of the tithe,
and it is the view of Abba Elazar ben Gomel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that Step 11 knocked down.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New re-defining of the case, tied to one תנא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about standard תרומה, which cannot explain ten figs.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is about תרומת מעשר, following אבא אלעזר בן גומל.

steps.title: The פסוק speaks about two kinds of תרומה
steps.stepSummary: אבא אלעזר בן גומל teaches that the פסוק 'ונחשב לכם תרומתכם' refers to both תרומה גדולה and תרומת מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: אבא אלעזר בן גומל says: 'And your תרומה shall be counted for you' — the פסוק speaks about two kinds of תרומה, standard תרומה and תרומת מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for אבא אלעזר בן גומל's view. He reads one פסוק as covering both kinds of תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because one פסוק covers both, the two kinds of תרומה are compared to each other. That comparison sets up the rule in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And your תרומה shall be counted for you' (במדבר 18:27)
The פסוק is speaking about

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: אַבָּא אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן גּוֹמֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught: Abba Elazar ben Gomel says:
"And your teruma shall be reckoned to you" –
the verse speaks about two terumot,
one is standard teruma
and one is teruma of the tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: אַבָּא אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן גּוֹמֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the view named in Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That אבא אלעזר בן גומל treats תרומת מעשר like standard תרומה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading במדבר 18:27 as covering two kinds of תרומה.

steps.title: תרומת מעשר may also be taken by estimate
steps.stepSummary: Just as standard תרומה can be taken by estimate and by thought, so too תרומת מעשר can be taken by estimate.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as standard תרומה may be taken by estimate and by thought, so too תרומת מעשר may be taken by estimate.
steps.whatsHappening: אבא אלעזר בן גומל gives the practical result of the comparison: תרומת מעשר, like standard תרומה, does not need an exact measurement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If תרומת מעשר may be taken by estimate, it does not have to be an exact tenth. That is why the answer in Step 12 can explain רבי יוסי's ten figs as תרומת מעשר, even though they are not a precise measure. אבא אלעזר בן גומל's statement continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Estimate; taking an amount by guessing rather than measuring exactly
Thought; setting it aside in one's mind
Just as... so too; a comparison between two cases

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the rule that lets the ברייתא make sense as a source about תרומת מעשר.

phrases.english: Just as standard teruma is taken
by estimate and by thought,
